DrawersPage.description:
Paginated response for GET /palace/{user_id}/drawers (M0.6.2).

A first-class response model rather than a raw dict because M0.12's
OpenAPI snapshot contract test captures whatever the route declares.
A route returning a bare dict renders as an empty object in the
generated schema, which would lock in "this endpoint has no
documented response" forever and silently pass every future
response-shape change.

``total`` is ``None`` whenever a wing/room filter is applied — the
honest-totals contract (see deltas "2026-04-20 list_drawers honest
totals"). Chroma's ``col.count()`` has no filter argument, so
returning an unfiltered total under a filter would be a
user-visible lie. ``None`` lets the Flask adapter render "showing
N of many" or omit the count.

``next_offset`` is ``None`` at end-of-pagination — either because
the current page was short (``len(drawers) < limit``) or because
``offset + limit >= total``. Callers iterate until they see
``next_offset is None``.
DrawersPage.title: DrawersPage

RebuildRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /palace/{user_id}/rebuild`` (M0.8).

``conversations`` is a list of ingest-shaped turns. Each is the
exact same wire shape as a normal ``/ingest`` request (reusing
``IngestRequest``) so the rebuild path and the normal ingest path
share validation and the handle's ``add_drawer`` call signature.

**Cap: 100 items per request** — spec §5.2 calls the route
"long-running, streaming" but M0.8 ships sync-POST (see deltas
2026-04-21 M0.8 rebuild-streaming deviation). A sync rebuild
holds the per-user writer_lock for the full duration; at ~100ms
per drawer, 100 conversations ~= 10s worst-case lock hold, which
is the ceiling that keeps parallel reads from timing out at
Flask's 2s client budget. The 501st item is rejected with HTTP
413; larger rebuilds land when streaming + ``from_path`` arrive
in a later milestone.
RebuildRequest.title: RebuildRequest

RebuildResponse.description:
Response for ``POST /palace/{user_id}/rebuild`` (M0.8).

``ingested`` counts ``AddDrawerResult.status == 'accepted'``;
``skipped`` counts ``'duplicate'``. Together they sum to
``len(request.conversations)``.

**No ``job_id`` in M0.8.** The earlier draft had a UUID4
``job_id`` field "forward-compatible with streaming." M0.8
quality review flagged it as dead weight with a silent-drift
risk: a caller seeing a UUID in the response reasonably assumes
polling semantics (standard job-queue idiom), and when streaming
lands and ``job_id`` becomes load-bearing, callers that already
started relying on it in M0.8 hit a silent contract change.
Dropped for M0.8; reintroduced when streaming ships and its
semantics are actually used.
RebuildResponse.title: RebuildResponse

get.description:
Prometheus scrape endpoint (spec §8.1).

Multiproc-aware: ``render_metrics`` branches on
``PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR`` — production (env set) aggregates
across uvicorn workers via ``MultiProcessCollector``; dev / unit
tests (env unset) fall back to the default registry with a
one-shot WARNING.

delete.description:
Two-phase destructive deletion of a user's palace.

Flow (spec §4.4 + plan M0.8.1):

  1. Check palace dir exists; 404 if not (already-deleted case
     must not silently recreate + delete-empty, which would
     muddy the audit trail).
  2. ``registry.open(user_id)`` to get the entry.
  3. Acquire the user's ``writer_lock``.
  4. Compute ``before_bytes`` from the palace dir.
  5. ``entry.handle.close()`` — pops the library backend cache
     per spec §5.3 contract.
  6. ``registry.evict(user_id)`` — removes from registry cache.
  7. ``os.replace`` to ``<dir>.pending_delete.<ts>`` — atomic;
     the palace is gone from the caller's perspective after this.
  8. ``asyncio.shield(audit.record_delete(...))`` — audit row
     lands even if the outer timeout fires during this step.
     rmtree is NOT shielded; a timeout mid-rmtree leaves the
     .pending_delete dir for the reaper to finish (spec §4.4).
  9. ``shutil.rmtree`` via ``asyncio.to_thread`` — fast for
     typical palaces; bounded by the 30s ``wait_for``.
  10. Return ``DeletionReceipt`` and increment
      ``mempalace_delete_total``.

Cancellation behavior: the route is wrapped in
``asyncio.wait_for(_, timeout=30.0)``. On timeout, CancelledError
propagates into whichever step was running, the writer_lock
releases, and we return HTTP 504. We do NOT catch CancelledError
inside the inner flow — let it propagate (FastAPI's default
handling surfaces it as 504 via wait_for's TimeoutError).

get.description:
Paginated GDPR-admin listing (plan M0.6.2).

Thin bridge over ``PalaceHandle.list_drawers``. Offset pagination
(ChromaDB's ``col.get`` has no cursor concept; see deltas
"2026-04-20 M0.3 library isolation", cursor → offset bullet).
``total`` is ``None`` when wing/room filter applies (honest-totals
contract). ``next_offset`` is ``None`` at end-of-pagination.

Read path, same reader_lock / asyncio.to_thread / 503 discipline
as /search above.

``limit`` default aligns to ``PalaceHandle.list_drawers``'s own
default (20); plan sketch's 100 predates the handle. Route bounds
``ge=1, le=200`` prevent a million-item request.

post.description:
Accept a single conversation turn and file it as a drawer.

Flow (spec §4.1 amended write-path ordering):

  1. Optional ``Idempotency-Key`` header parsing. If present AND
     differs from ``body.turn_id``, return 400 — the header is a
     contract-assertion channel for catching outbox bugs, not a
     dedup mechanism. Either way, we stash it in the structured
     log for correlation with Flask's outbox.

  2. ``registry.open(user_id)`` — opens (or fetches cached) the
     per-user palace. May trigger eviction of a different user;
     that's fine, it runs under its own lock.

  3. ``async with lock.writer_lock:`` — serialises this write
     against any other writer for the same user_id (spec §5.3
     invariant: "caller holds the per-user write lock for mutating
     methods"). Parallel readers on the same user still proceed
     under the reader_lock.

  4. ``handle.add_drawer(...)`` — wrapped in ``asyncio.to_thread``
     to keep the event loop responsive while the synchronous
     SELECT + library call + INSERT executes. The call is usually
     fast (local sqlite + Chroma upsert), but "usually fast" isn't
     a concurrency story — blocking the loop on every ingest would
     stall every other route.

  5. Return ``IngestResponse(status=result.status)`` — ``accepted``
     means a fresh row landed in turns.sqlite; ``duplicate`` means
     the turn_id was already present. No 3rd status exists.

Rebuild a user's palace from a list of conversations (plan
M0.8.2).

Sync-POST flow: iterate ``body.conversations``, call
``handle.add_drawer`` for each under writer_lock. Idempotent by
``turn_id`` per M0.4 contract — re-runs of the same conversation
list report all-skipped on the second call.

Hold-time bound: writer_lock is held for the full loop
(~100ms/drawer at ingest rates). The 100-conversation cap
(deviation #7) keeps worst-case hold under ~10s, below Flask's
2s client-side read budget with margin. Larger rebuilds require
streaming + ``from_path`` (deferred to a later milestone); spec
§5.2 "long-running, streaming" language is what that milestone
will satisfy. See deltas for the streaming-deferral entry.

Tool-call search over a user's palace (plan M0.6.1).

Thin bridge over ``PalaceHandle.search`` — library-owned hybrid
BM25 + vector + closet-boost retrieval with optional wing filter.
Read path, reader_lock (NOT writer_lock). Synchronous library
call goes through ``asyncio.to_thread`` so the event loop stays
responsive for parallel readers under the same user and for
every other user on the worker.

503 on ``registry.open`` raising "shutting down" — mirrors the
ingest/wake-up pattern so load-balancers classify correctly.

schema.title: Response Search Palace  User Id  Search Post

post.description:
Assemble the four-layer wake-up context (L0/L1/L2/L3) for a
user turn. HOT READ path — every turn hits this before the LLM.

Flow (spec §4.2 read path A):

  1. ``registry.open(user_id, track_cold=True)`` — returns the
     cached ``PalaceEntry`` or opens a fresh palace if cold. The
     ``was_cold`` flag propagates into ``WakeupMeta.hot`` so the
     caller (Flask adapter, M0.17) can render latency expectations.

  2. If ``?warmup=true``, return an empty ``WakeupContext`` —
     the purpose of the request was to move the palace into the
     cache, NOT to run the composition. Useful for pre-turn
     background warmup from the Flask adapter.

  3. Otherwise acquire ``registry.lock_for(user_id).reader_lock``
     (NOT writer_lock — wake-up is a READ) and call
     ``build_wakeup``. Parallel wake-ups for the same user run
     concurrently under the reader_lock; concurrent writers
     (ingest) serialise against readers via the writer_lock.

  4. Any ``RuntimeError`` containing "shutting down" from the
     registry maps to HTTP 503 (mirrors the ingest pattern).

user_id is logged pseudonymously per spec §8.4 (sha256+salt).

get.description:
Readiness gate (spec §8.1 alert ``MempalaceReadyzFailing``).

Returns ``ok=True`` iff:
  - ``app.state.embedding_ready`` is True (lifespan step 1
    completed the ``prime_embedding_function`` warm-up).
  - ``app.state.registry`` is attached (lifespan step 2).
  - ``app.state.audit`` is attached (lifespan step 2b).
  - ``app.state.accepting`` is True (M0.10 shutdown gate not
    flipped).
  - ``app.state._shutdown_done`` is not True (shutdown_sequence
    has not run yet).

The shutdown-gate checks deviate from the plan's ``shutting_down``
attribute — plan predates M0.10; this route uses the actual
attributes M0.10 ships (see deltas 2026-04-21 M0.11 deviation #1).

``readyz_gauge`` is set to 1/0 so the
``MempalaceReadyzFailing`` alert fires on the scrape output
even during the window between a degradation and the next
``/readyz`` probe.
